sections.html:
Of all the municipalities in Prince George's County, Bowie is the largest, home to 58,329 people in 20,991 households as of 2020. Most homes sit in the Levitt-planned community built in the 1960s, after Levitt and Sons bought the Belair Estate in 1957 and the city annexed the land in 1959. Old Town Bowie, the original railroad junction settlement, is the older core.

So many houses date from the same decade that buyers line one up against its neighbors. Be ready for questions about the roof, windows, kitchen and whatever else has or has not been updated. Some owners live near listed historic sites such as Belair Mansion, the Bowie Railroad Buildings, Sacred Heart Catholic Church and Melford. Ask the city and county whether any historic-property rules apply before you plan exterior work.

A Bowie house is billed by the city and the county, with state and regional charges added. These are the fiscal 2026 figures.

ChargeRate per $100 of assessed value
City of Bowie$0.8760
Prince George's County$1.0000
State of Maryland$0.1120
M-NCPPC$0.2940
Washington Suburban Transit Commission$0.0260

County rates are reduced inside incorporated areas, so ask the Treasury office which figure fits your address. At closing the settlement agent pays the bill out of your proceeds, which means you only need this year's payoff number.

The county mails its bill in July. Pay it all by September 30, or, if it is your principal residence, pay half by then and half by December 31.

You can pay the county by web, phone, mail or at the counter. Web fees: $1.50 on an e-check, $3.95 on a Visa debit card, 2.45% on any other card. By phone, dial 855-516-1830 (extra fees apply).

  • By mail, send the stub to P.O. Box 37050, New York, NY 10087.
  • In person, go to 1301 McCormick Drive, Suite 1100, Largo, weekdays 9:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. The counter takes no cash.
  • A walk-up slot open around the clock accepts checks, money orders and cashier's checks.

The bill can also carry a Front Foot Benefit charge for sewer or water pipes in the street (WSSC, 301-206-8032) or a solid waste charge. Ask the title company to include both in the payoff.

sections.h2: Unpaid taxes and the county tax sale
sections.html:
Whatever is still owed on the second Monday in May goes up for bid at the county's yearly tax sale, and the highest bidder takes the lien. Interest and penalty run 1.67% per month while a balance sits, and not receiving a bill does not excuse it.

Treasury Customer Service, 301-952-4030, gives payoff figures. Being behind does not block a sale as long as the arrears come out of the sale price. With the May date weeks away, tell the buyer and title company right away so they order the payoff in time.

sections.h2: Selling a house with back taxes
sections.html:
Here is how it normally runs. You request a payoff, the title company confirms every lien, and the closing agent pays the county out of your proceeds, then wires you what is left. When the price covers the debt, you bring no money to the table.

When a tax sale date looms, a cash buyer's lack of a lender helps: no appraisal, no underwriting. Every lien must still be cleared before recording, so start with your latest tax bill and any notices.

Rental licensing for Bowie addresses comes from the city, not the county. The county sends owners to the state's real property search: when the Town column reads Bowie, the license application goes to Bowie.

If a former rental has a license problem or an unpermitted conversion, resolve it before a sale. County code compliance enforces its rules through a Notice of Violation or a Civil Citation. Ask the city which office handles code complaints for a property inside Bowie.

Prince George's County charges 1.4% transfer tax and $2.75 recordation tax per $500 of consideration, and the state adds 0.5% on transfer.

Your contract assigns each share. Full figures appear on the settlement statement the title company prints, so request a draft days ahead and compare it with the contract.

Under Maryland Real Property Code 10-702, anyone selling one to four units hands the buyer either a condition disclosure or a disclaimer on or before the day of contract signing. Choosing the disclaimer means the house goes as-is, apart from latent defects the seller actually knows about. Bank-owned foreclosures, tax sales, estates and trusts do not have to use the form.

Sellers who choose the disclaimer still answer for known latent defects, so list anything you know about, such as past leaks or a failing furnace.

Take photo ID, keys, garage remotes and any manuals or warranties for the furnace, water heater and appliances. The closing agent already has the payoff letters, deed and settlement statement. Go through the statement one line at a time, checking that taxes, transfer charges and bill adjustments match your contract.

After signing, the deed goes to the land records and the county updates the owner of record. Forward any mail from the Treasury office to the new owner or to your new address, so a stray bill does not follow you. Keep your closing papers for at least the next tax season in case a question about proration comes up.

Paying cash removes the appraisal, the loan underwriting and the financing contingency, which are the usual reasons deals fall apart late. Inspections and title searches can still happen. If your Bowie house has an older kitchen, an aging roof or years as a rental, expect a firm date and little haggling over repair credits. Disclose what you know either way.

Two highways, I-595 and US 50 (the John Hanson Highway), cross the city east to west toward Washington and Annapolis. US 301 and MD 3 hug the east side on the way to Waldorf, La Plata and Baltimore. State routes 197, 214, 450 and 564 fill in the rest, and the MARC Penn Line stops at Bowie State. Commuters care about this, so say it in your listing.

Public schools belong to Prince George's County Public Schools. Bowie High is the high school, and the middle schools are Benjamin Tasker and Samuel Ogle.

sections.h2: Steps to a fast Bowie sale
sections.html:
1. Ask county Treasury for this year's payoff figure.
  2. Check for an open rental license problem or code notice.
  3. Fill in the disclosure or disclaimer form.
  4. Put the split of transfer and recordation tax in the contract.
  5. Review the settlement statement, sign and hand over the keys.

faqs.q: What is the Bowie, MD property tax rate?
faqs.a: Bowie's city rate for fiscal 2026 is $0.8760 per $100 of assessed value. County is $1.0000 (reduced for incorporated areas) and state is $0.1120.

faqs.q: When are property taxes due in Bowie?
faqs.a: Full payment to Prince George's County is due September 30. Principal residences can pay half by September 30 and half by December 31.

faqs.q: Does the county or the city license my Bowie rental?
faqs.a: The city does. The county leaves licensing to Bowie for addresses inside city limits.

faqs.q: What happens if I do not pay Bowie property taxes?
faqs.a: A balance still open on the second Monday in May is offered at the county's yearly tax sale, and it grows 1.67% each month until then.

faqs.q: How much is the transfer tax in Bowie?
faqs.a: Expect 1.4% county plus 0.5% state transfer tax, and $2.75 recordation per $500. The settlement agent can confirm who pays what.
